quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: Hummingbirds are the only birds that can fly backwards! They can also hover in place by flapping their wings in a figure-eight pattern up to 80 times per second. These tiny acrobats need to eat every 10-15 minutes to fuel their incredible energy needs.

short_read.title: The Secret Lives of Tide Pools
short_read.teaser: Tide pools along the Pacific Coast are miniature worlds filled with colorful sea stars, anemones, and tiny crabs. Discover what makes these rocky shoreline habitats so special and resilient.

medium_read.title: Budapest's Thermal Baths: A Living Tradition
medium_read.teaser: For over 2,000 years, Hungarians have gathered in thermal baths to relax, socialize, and heal. This beautiful photo essay explores the history and architecture of Budapest's famous bathhouses.

long_read.title: The Olympic Peninsula: Where Rainforest Meets the Sea
long_read.teaser: The Olympic Peninsula is one of the most ecologically diverse places on Earth, home to ancient rainforests, glacier-capped mountains, and rugged coastline. Learn how this unique landscape was formed and why it's unlike anywhere else.

port_angeles.title: Harbor Seal Pupping Season
port_angeles.description: August is peak harbor seal pupping season in the Strait of Juan de Fuca! Mother seals often rest with their pups on beaches and rocks near Port Angeles. Remember to keep at least 100 yards away so mothers don't abandon their babies.

puzzle_1.question: A ruby-throated hummingbird's heart beats about ___ times per minute when active.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Exactly right, Barbara! That tiny heart works incredibly hard — faster than you can even count!
puzzle_1.close_response: Very close! A hummingbird's heart beats about 1,200 times per minute — that's 20 beats every second!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: Those tiny hearts are amazing — they beat about 1,200 times per minute when the bird is active. That's more than 20 times faster than a human heart!
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: To fuel this incredible heart rate, hummingbirds must consume about half their body weight in sugar each day, visiting hundreds of flowers from dawn to dusk.

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'thank you'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Köszönöm, that's right! You know your Hungarian well, Ildiko!
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The word for 'thank you' is 'köszönöm' (or the shorter 'köszi'). Szia means 'hi,' igen means 'yes,' and kérem means 'please.'
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Hungarian is unique among European languages — it's part of the Finno-Ugric family, making it related to Finnish and Estonian rather than neighboring Slavic languages.

puzzle_3.question: What type of tree is the most common in Olympic National Park's temperate rainforest?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Beautiful! Sitka spruce trees dominate the rainforest, growing over 300 feet tall in the misty valleys. Their ability to thrive in wet conditions makes them perfect for this rainy climate.
puzzle_3.wrong_response: It's the Sitka spruce! These magnificent trees can grow over 300 feet tall and are perfectly adapted to the Olympic rainforest's wet climate. Some are over 500 years old.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: The Hoh Rain Forest in Olympic National Park receives up to 14 feet of rain annually, making it one of the wettest places in the continental United States and creating ideal conditions for these towering spruce trees.
